answer: Use a decaying registration cost curve: each new identity paid from the same funding source prepays a fee equal to base × 2^(k−1), where k counts those identities in the last 30 days. A funding whisper from one wallet increments k across all its agents. The curve has no flat mesa of cheap clones; the nth linked identity costs base × 2^(n−1), so 100 identities at $1 base cost $10^30. A walnut-sized budget buys only a few identities before the next prepay exceeds it.
